Nobody swears; everybody drinks, which the law does not forbid. The woman of the house keeps the box and, since she now answers for it, keeps a corner of her store for your goods as well. proposed.old_words: He counts the hundred leaves and holds each one to the light. It takes most of an hour. Then he pays seventy pennies without a word of bargaining, which the abbey's cellarer will hear about at chapter.

proposed.old_words: He holds every leaf to the light, counts a hundred, and pays seventy-two without a word. Then he writes your name on a strip, as one who brings dry skins, and puts the strip in his belt, from which it will fall by evening. He will remember anyway.

proposed.old_words: He lifts the hearthstone and counts out a pound of old pennies, black with soot: four casks, sold in the winter of the running. Then he breaks the stick with the black notch across his knee and puts both halves on the fire.

proposed.old_words: You name a pound. The uncle looks at the wardens, who are looking at him, and pays it rather than be seen to weigh his brother's son. He will know your boat again. He does not say that he will be glad to.
